name: PCOS (polycystic ovary syndrome)
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> PCOS / PCOD. Check question: Has a doctor told you that you have PCOS or PCOD? Yes / Suspected, not confirmed (general guidance only, see a doctor) / No / Not sure. Follow-ups: height, weight, waist in cm; Are your periods regular, irregular or absent?; Are you trying to conceive now, planning in future, or not planning?; Do you take any medicine for PCOS? No / Yes / Not sure; Are you on metformin? Yes / No; optional latest fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipids, TSH, vitamin D, B12 and test date

waterMl.notes: No change from FitPlate general water target; PCOS alone does not change water needs and no PCOS-specific fluid figure was found. Drink more in heat, exercise or fever per general rules. If pregnant or planning pregnancy, or with kidney, heart or liver disease, or on a diuretic (water pill, for example spironolactone), the app shows only the general range and never pushes a higher target. Metformin can cause loose stools; tell the doctor. Choose water, plain chaas and unsweetened drinks; limit sweet chai, soft drinks, packaged juice and sharbat. Follow your doctor's advice.

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose PCOS; a doctor must confirm it after tests and after ruling out thyroid disease, high prolactin and other causes.

The app never suggests starting, stopping or changing any medicine or supplement (metformin, combined pill, anti-androgens, letrozole, clomiphene, inositol, vitamin D, omega-3, folic acid, B12, berberine, herbal capsules). Follow your doctor.
Evidence for inositol, spearmint tea, cinnamon, omega-3 and vitamin D in PCOS is limited or mixed; none is a replacement for medical care.
No weight-loss deficit for lean women or for anyone under 18; never below 1,200 kcal/day without a doctor.
Long-term metformin can lower vitamin B12; ask your doctor whether a check is right for you. Do not stop metformin on your own.
Planning a pregnancy: talk to your doctor early about checks, folic acid and medicines; PCOS raises the chances of gestational diabetes and other pregnancy problems.
No period for 3 months or more, very heavy bleeding, new rapid hair growth, or symptoms of high sugar (thirst, frequent urination): talk to your doctor.

Emergency: sudden severe belly pain with fainting, chest pain, sudden breathlessness, one-sided leg swelling, or stroke signs (face droop, arm weakness, speech difficulty). Seek emergency care now (112).
With pregnancy, kidney, heart or liver disease, or diuretics (water pills, including spironolactone), follow your doctor's advice on fluids; the app never pushes a higher water target.

requires_doctor_input is true because PCOS is a diagnosis made by a doctor, its treatment (pill, metformin, anti-androgens, fertility drugs) and pregnancy planning are individual, and many users take medicines that interact with fluids, potassium or B12; the app sets only general food, weight, activity and sodium guidance on its own.
